questions.q: You ran mv draft.conf bazaar.conf. bazaar.conf already existed. What happened to it?
options: It was replaced silently by draft.conf
questions.explain: cp and mv overwrite without asking. Use -i (ask) or -n (never overwrite), and cp file file.bak before editing.

questions.q: mkdir backups/2026/11 fails with No such file or directory. Why, and what's the fix?
options: Folders can't have numbers; rename them
backups/2026 doesn't exist yet; use mkdir -p backups/2026/11
questions.explain: -p creates all missing parent folders, and doesn't complain if they already exist.

questions.q: ls shows logs, config and media. Where is the .env file?
options: It's a hidden file (its name starts with a dot); ls -a shows it
Only root can see it with ls
questions.explain: Files whose names start with . are hidden by default. ls -a shows all files.

questions.q: Which command shows new lines of live.log as the backend writes them?
questions.explain: tail -f follows the file until you press Ctrl+C. Inside less, F does the same.

questions.q: The disk is almost full. Which one-liner shows what fills the current folder, biggest last?
questions.explain: du measures each item's size; sort -h orders human sizes like 20K, 48K, 12M. Then cd into the biggest and repeat.

questions.q: You opened a file in vi and typed some text by mistake. How do you leave without saving?
options: Press Esc, then type :q! and Enter
questions.explain: Esc returns to normal mode; :q! quits without saving. :wq saves and quits; i starts typing.

questions.q: (Going deeper) What does mv do on disk when you rename a file in the same folder?
options: Copies all the data to a new place
Changes only the name; the inode and data stay where they are
Deletes the file and creates a new one
questions.explain: That's why mv is instant even for huge files. cp creates a new inode with a full copy.

questions.q: (Going deeper) A backup script copies with cp -a, then deletes all but the 3 newest using ls -t. It deletes the newest backup. Why?
options: cp -a keeps the original's modification time, so all backups have the same time and ls -t can't order them
questions.explain: Put a sortable timestamp (YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS) in the name and sort by name instead.
